B. Tax instalments for the year ending December 31, 2027

The CRA wants the corporation to pay its tax a little each month, not all at once after the year ends. These payments are called instalments.

Last year, the corporation's tax was more than $3,000. When that happens, the CRA asks for these payments the next year.

These payments are not extra tax. They count toward the corporation's tax for the year ending December 31, 2027. If you skip them, the CRA charges interest.

The payments are $700 a month starting in January. January to March have passed, so the first payment catches up 3 months: 3 x $700 = $2,100. The CRA may still charge a small amount of interest on those late months.

Instalment due dates

  • March 31, 2027: $2,100
  • April 30, 2027: $700
  • May 31, 2027: $700

Pay instalments to the same RC 0001 account and choose "instalment" as the payment type.

C. How to pay

Pay through your online banking or through CRA My Payment on the CRA website. Each amount above is its own payment.

D. Your documents

Your compiled financial statements, full T2 return, signed T183CORP, CRA e-file confirmation and minute book letter (please forward it to your lawyer) are in your TaxDome portal. The CRA requires you to keep them for 6 years.
